frameworks.name: Stone Cutter Parable
frameworks.definition: A framework for reframing identical work through three different perspectives: pain-focused, family-focused, and purpose-focused — demonstrating that outlook determines bearability.

frameworks.name: Time Bifurcation Model
frameworks.definition: Allocating daily time into two blocks: high-intensity focus on one core skill (sales, 8-10 hours), and secondary learning/entrepreneurship (5 a.m.-9 a.m., 5 p.m.-9 p.m.) plus weekends.

frameworks.name: Ten Stage Revenue Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A scaling framework outlining predictable stages from zero to $100M+ revenue, broken down by eight business functions and symptoms at each stage.

claims.text: The vast majority of daily work in any business—even one built around passion—will not be doing the thing you love; most of the day will be administrative, operational, or logistical work unrelated to the passionate core.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: When you scale a business, the ratio of core-passion work to supporting work compresses (core work stays roughly constant while supporting work grows with scale).

numbers.axis: percentage of workday devoted to passion activity

bounded_by: Does not apply to pure hobby work where there is no business model to build

claims.text: If you performed the same activity you currently enjoy every single day—without breaks and as paid work—you would eventually stop enjoying it because human adaptation makes rarity and choice the source of enjoyment, not the activity itself.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Hedonic adaptation: humans derive pleasure from novelty and volition; repetition at scale removes both, flattening enjoyment regardless of the activity type.
bounded_by: Does not apply to activities where the reward structure includes external validation or advancement (e.g., competitive sports where ranking provides novelty)

claims.text: Reframing work from 'I hate this task' to 'I am providing for people I care about' or 'I am building something that lasts' changes the bearability and meaning of identical work without changing the work itself.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: when the work genuinely serves others or builds lasting value
when the reframe is internally endorsed, not imposed
claims.mechanism: Outlook determines emotional response; the same physical activity feels different depending on the narrative frame applied to it, and the human nervous system responds to narrative meaning, not objective task difficulty.

claims.text: A young person earning money through cold-call sales while supporting their family is performing an act of honor equivalent to rice farmers providing for their families in ancient China—the honor comes from the sacrifice for others, not the pleasantness of the work.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: when the work genuinely supports dependents
when the person consciously recognizes the sacrifice
claims.mechanism: Social/biological meaning: humans are wired to find meaning and status in providing for in-group members; recognizing this wiring makes difficult work feel purposeful.

claims.text: A founder who follows their passion and discovers that 80-95% of the resulting business work is unrelated to that passion was not deceived by the passion—they were deceived by the expectation that passion would translate into daily practice.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Business scaling requires breadth of activities (sales, operations, marketing, finance) regardless of domain; passion is a north star, not a daily practice descriptor.

numbers.axis: percentage of workday aligned with founder's stated passion

anchors.value: 5-10% of day (rest: membership sales, floor cleaning, billing, playlist selection, marketing)

claims.text: To escape poverty while learning desired skills, allocate peak cognitive hours (8-10 hours) to mastering one high-leverage skill (cold-call sales), and use remaining discretionary time (5 a.m.-9 a.m., 5 p.m.-9 p.m., weekends) to learn secondary skills (AI, creative) and apply them via the primary skill leverage.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: for someone in poverty without capital
with available hours outside of employment
when a high-leverage income skill (sales) exists
claims.mechanism: Sales skill is universally applicable across domains; learning it first creates optionality and leverage for secondary skills; using discretionary hours prevents false choice between income and learning.

anchors.region: peak hours for primary skill mastery

anchors.value: 5 a.m.-9 a.m. (4 hours) + 5 p.m.-9 p.m. (4 hours) + weekends

bounded_by: Does not apply if the primary income is not scalable or teachable (e.g., manual labor with no learning curve)

claims.text: Learning to sell through cold calling is a core life competency applicable across all future endeavors, regardless of whether technology automates cold calling in the future.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: applies to anyone building a business or career
applies to leadership and influence requirements
claims.mechanism: Selling is fundamentally about communication, persuasion, handling rejection, and persistence; these are universal human skills that transfer to all domains.

claims.text: Work is inherently hard; the difference between bearable and unbearable is narrative framing, not objective difficulty.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: The nervous system responds to meaning, not just stimulus; identical difficulty feels different depending on whether the person believes the work serves a purpose.

claims.text: The revenue scaling roadmap from zero to $100M+ has predictable stages that less than 1% of companies complete; each stage has characteristic constraints, symptoms, and graduation requirements across eight business functions (the roadmap is domain-agnostic).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: applies across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar
applies to ventures aiming for nine-figure scale
claims.mechanism: Scaling follows predictable inflection points where the binding constraint shifts (founder capacity → team capacity → market capacity); knowing these in advance allows pre-positioning.

numbers.axis: percentage of companies completing the full roadmap

examples.text: Alex Hormozi started his career as a management consultant and finance professional pursuing a 'make money' track. He then switched to fitness—his lifelong passion—and started a gym. Once the gym was operational, he discovered that his daily work consisted of selling memberships, cleaning equipment, mopping floors, marketing, playlist selection, and billing—none of which was the fitness training he had been passionate about.

A question-asker (age 21, broke, supporting his mom) works cold calls which he hates. He wants to learn AI and creative design. Hormozi reframes the cold-calling work as an honorable act of family provision (equivalent to ancient rice farmers), then offers a dual-track plan: master cold-calling (8-10 hours daily), and learn AI/creative in 5-9 a.m. and 5-9 p.m. blocks to practice applied sales in new domains.

The parable of the stone cutter: three workers perform identical stone-hammering work. The first complains it is backbreaking drudgery. The second says he is providing for his family. The third says he is building a cathedral that will last generations. All three do the same work, but their emotional experience and motivation differ entirely based on their narrative frame.

practices.text: When facing work you dislike, explicitly adopt a narrative frame that connects the work to a larger purpose (family provision, lasting creation, skill development) rather than focusing only on the task itself.

Double down and develop mastery in a high-leverage skill (sales, negotiation, communication) before diversifying into secondary interests; the primary skill creates optionality and leverage for all future work.

Use discretionary time blocks (early morning, evening, weekends) to learn and practice secondary skills while maintaining peak cognitive hours for primary income-generating work; this avoids the false choice between financial survival and skill development.

Recognize that passion-driven work will still consist mostly of unglamorous operational tasks; accept this and focus on mastery and meaning in the operational work itself, not on waiting for the 'fun' part to materialize.
